title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Solut. 1: A universal cause still needs each one’s application by faith
pass_a_gloss: We acknowledge the fullest sufficiency of the ransom (lytri), yes even its infinite superabundance: but we answer, This merit of Christ considered in itself alone operates indeed sufficiently as a universal cause of human salvation; but a universal cause does not produce effects in singulars before singular application (applicationem). By the death of Christ itself therefore there has been instituted a most sufficient universal cause, from which (as Aquinas speaks) whatsoever sins of whomsoever could be expiated; but before this cause puts forth its expiatory force toward liberation and reconciliation of singulars, it must be applied to each by faith. Which the Apostle himself clearly taught Rom. 3:25. Whom God set forth as a propitiatory through faith in his blood, etc. Although therefore this death of Christ is a sufficient satisfaction for the sins of the human race, yet since by way of a remedy it cleanses us from sins, it must first be applied to each one before it can produce the effect of reconciliation and health (sanitatis): But application is not made except through faith.
pass_b_english: We acknowledge the fullest sufficiency of the ransom—indeed its infinite superabundance. Our answer, however, is this: Christ's merit, considered in itself alone, does operate sufficiently as a universal cause of human salvation; yet a universal cause does not produce effects in particular persons before it is applied to each one. By Christ's death itself, therefore, a most sufficient universal cause was instituted, from which (as Aquinas says) any sins of any persons could be expiated. But before that cause puts forth its expiatory power for the liberation and reconciliation of individuals, it must be applied to each by faith. The Apostle himself teaches this clearly in Romans 3:25: "Whom God set forth as a propitiatory through faith in his blood," and so on.

So although Christ's death is a sufficient satisfaction for the sins of the human race, it cleanses us by way of a remedy: it must first be applied to each person before it can produce the effect of reconciliation and healing. And that application is made only through faith.
source_text: Agnoscimus plenissimam lytri sufficientiam, imo infinitam ejusdem superabundantiam: sed respondemus, Hoc meritum Christi in se solo consideratum operari quidem sufficienter, ut causam salutis humanae universalem; universalis autem causa non producit effectus in singularibus ante singularem applicationem. Ipsa igitur morte Christi instituta est causa universalis sufficientissima, ex qua (ut loquitur Aquinas) possent quaecunque quorumcunque peccata expiari; sed priusquam haec causa vim suam exserat expiatoriam ad liberationem & reconciliationem singulorum, oportet eam applicari singulis per fidem. Quod ipse Apostolus perspicue docuit Rom. iii. 25. Quem proposuit Deus propitiatorium per fidem in sanguine ipsius, &c. Quamvis ergo haec mors Christi sit sufficiens satisfactio pro peccatis humani generis, cum tamen per modum remedii nos purget a peccatis, est unicuique prius applicanda, quam possit effectum reconciliationis & sanitatis producere: Applicatio autem non fit nisi per fidem.
